result.title: Toward Collective Model Intelligence: Characterizing and Coordinating Models
result.summary: Independently developed AI models accumulate diverse and complementary capabilities, but a growing model collection does not automatically realize Collective AI. Addressing this gap requires understanding model capabilities with limited evaluation, organizing complementary models to collaborate on diverse tasks, and executing model calls efficiently under resource constraints. We present a systematic approach to pursuing Collective Model Intelligence through three connected components. First, Model Eval constructs evidence-based capability profiles by combining query-level performance estimation with cross-domain prediction, reducing the need for exhaustive evaluation. Second, Mio (Models in One) organizes complementary model candidates and supports task-conditioned, cost-aware selection and collaboration as task requirements evolve. Third, Mos (Model Serving OS) separates model selection from execution and provides endpoint scheduling and shared model deployment and distribution. Experiments show lower capability-estimation errors under limited evaluation. Across nine public benchmarks, Mio 1.0 Lite achieves the highest average score and lowest average cost among compared methods, with per-request costs 73.7-97.5% lower than those of the best-scoring alternatives. A prewarmed shared cache accelerates model-file retrieval by up to 23.3 times. This work lays a foundation for Collective Model Intelligence by characterizing and coordinating the diverse capabilities of an expanding model universe.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 Collective Model Intelligence 框架，包含基于有限评测的能力画像（Model Eval）、按任务需求与成本组织模型协作的选择模块（Mio）以及分离选择与执行的模型服务系统（Mos）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「有限评测推断能力＋按成本动态选择协作对象」的思路，可能为 LVR 中依据任务需求动态分配 latent 计算、决定证据来源与停止时机提供类比线索，但原文不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态，可供核查的具体迁移点较弱。
